slides.title: Shortline
slides.subtitle: Live wait-time predictions for campus dining halls, from Wi-Fi occupancy counts
slides.byline: Ana Ruiz · Wei Chen · Sam Okafor — Fall 2026
slides.notes: Open with the one-liner, then go straight to the problem. 20 seconds.

slides.title: Students lose 20+ minutes a day guessing which dining hall is quiet
slides.body: Today the workaround is walking over and looking. Our intake survey (n=64) found 71% had left a line without eating at least once this term.
slides.notes: Cite the survey size. Judges will ask how the 64 were recruited: dorm group chats, so skewed to first-years.

slides.title: From access-point counts to a 15-minute forecast
slides.caption: Everything solid black runs in the demo today. Dashed boxes are not built yet and are not shown.
slides.notes: Point at the dashed boxes yourself before a judge does.

slides.title: Why gradient boosting instead of an LSTM

left.label: Considered
left.title: LSTM sequence model
points: Needs months of history we don't have
Harder to explain a bad forecast

right.label: Chose
right.title: LightGBM on lag features
points: Trains in 40 s on a laptop
Beat LSTM baseline on our 6-week holdout

slides.verdict: Revisit sequence models once a full semester of data exists.

slides.title: Pick a hall at 11:50 on a Tuesday
steps: Open the widget: three halls, current wait and 15-minute forecast
Replay last Tuesday's lunch rush from the recorded feed
Show the forecast catching the 12:05 spike four minutes early
Open the admin view: per-hall error over the last week
slides.fallback: Recorded 90-second screen capture of the same flow, on the desktop as shortline-demo.mp4

rows.criterion: Live AP counts for ≥2 halls by week 4

slides.title: What broke, and what we learned

cards.title: Event days
cards.body: Career fairs and home games push error past 8 minutes. We have no event feed yet.

cards.title: AP coverage
cards.body: One access point covers two rooms in IV, so counts overstate the line.

cards.title: Users want 'go now / wait'
cards.body: Interviews (n=12) showed a number in minutes was less useful than a simple call.
